items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-06-20
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...What's the thing about, William? [INTERVIEWEE] You know, uh, there was nobody better than Earl Palmer...

ctx.x: Well, well, well. What should a drummer be doing? First of all, he got to have two good hands. Uh-huh. See, because you need the solid back beat thing. You need the 6-8 rhythm. So these are two things that got to be going together. Uh-huh. Okay. Uh, if he ain't got but one hand, naturally, he ain't gonna play most likely the 6-8 because that's where it comes from that left hand. He might have, he might, now my drummer cannot play the back beat. I told him last night. I said, man, you play the back beat like as if…
Who's your favorite drummer? Who could play? Right now, today? No, not today. What's the thing about, William?

You know, uh, there was nobody better than Earl Palmer, man, for recording, for whatever. You know, I remember Earl, Earl one time, we was in the Dew Drop, and this drummer came down here. He OD'd. He came down here with Roy Brown. Heck of a drummer. I can't remember his name. But boy, he could play. But boy, he could play. And so, one night, we was all in the Dew Drop listening to him. And, uh, when he finished, I told Earl, I said, why don't you go ahead and sit in, man? He said, man, the captain played…
